## Purpose
`verify_equal_vocab_size_if_draft_model()` only enforced vocabulary parity when `method == "draft_model"`, silently skipping `eagle` and `eagle3`.  A mismatched vocabulary between target and draft model causes out-of-bounds GPU memory access during speculative decoding.

Fixes #34583.

This continues the work started in #34722 (closed without merge), using a minimal patch to the existing method rather than introducing a new one.

## Test Plan                                                                                                                                                                                                             
`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_verify_vocab_size_raises_for_eagle_mismatch tests/test_config.py::test_verify_vocab_size_allows_eagle3_pruned_vocab -v`

## Test Result
```
test_verify_vocab_size_raises_for_eagle_mismatch[eagle] PASSED
test_verify_vocab_size_raises_for_eagle_mismatch[eagle3] PASSED 
test_verify_vocab_size_allows_eagle3_pruned_vocab PASSED
3 passed in 1.82s
```

## Code Review

This pull request extends vocabulary size validation in SpeculativeConfig to include the eagle and eagle3 methods, while introducing an exception for pruned vocabularies when draft_vocab_size is defined in the configuration. New unit tests verify these validation rules. Reviewers suggested including the dflash method in the validation logic and associated tests to ensure consistency and prevent potential memory access issues.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `dflash` speculative method also utilizes a draft model and is susceptible to the same out-of-bounds memory access issues if the vocabulary size is mismatched. It should be included in this validation check for consistency and safety.

```suggestion
            self.method in ("draft_model", "eagle", "eagle3", "dflash")
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Consider adding `dflash` to the parametrized test cases to ensure it is also correctly validated for vocabulary parity.

```suggestion
@pytest.mark.parametrize("method", ["eagle", "eagle3", "dflash"])
```

nodes.body:
## Code Review

This pull request extends vocabulary size validation in SpeculativeConfig to include eagle and eagle3 methods, while allowing for intentional pruning when draft_vocab_size is present in the configuration. It also includes new test cases to verify these validation rules. Feedback suggests generalizing the validation logic to apply whenever both target and draft model configurations are available, rather than relying on a hardcoded list of methods, to ensure consistency across all speculative decoding types and improve maintainability.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The vocabulary size validation is currently restricted to a hardcoded list of methods (`draft_model`, `eagle`, `eagle3`). This excludes other speculative decoding methods that utilize a draft model, such as `dflash` and `mtp` (which are also part of `EagleModelTypes`), as well as `medusa` and `mlp_speculator`. If any of these methods are used with a mismatched vocabulary, it could still lead to the out-of-bounds GPU memory access issue this PR aims to prevent.

A more robust and maintainable approach is to perform this check whenever both `target_model_config` and `draft_model_config` are present. This automatically covers all current and future draft-based methods while remaining a no-op for methods like `ngram` where the configurations are identical.

```suggestion
            self.target_model_config is not None
            and self.draft_model_config is not None
```

It also adds corresponding unit tests. The reviewer recommends using self.use_eagle() to ensure all relevant methods like mtp and dflash are included in the validation.

The list of methods that require vocabulary size validation is incomplete. Other eagle-like methods such as `mtp` and `dflash` (which are part of `EagleModelTypes`) should also be included to prevent potential out-of-bounds access if their vocabularies are mismatched. Since `self.use_eagle()` already covers `eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, and `dflash`, it is cleaner and more robust to use it here.

```suggestion
            self.method == "draft_model" or self.use_eagle()
```

files.patch:
@@ -5,7 +5,7 @@
 import os
 from dataclasses import MISSING, Field, asdict, dataclass, field
 from types import SimpleNamespace
-from unittest.mock import patch
+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
 
 import pydantic
 import pytest
@@ -1467,3 +1467,43 @@ def test_ir_op_priority_ctx():
         # context restored even after exception
         assert ir.ops.rms_norm.get_priority() == ["vllm_c", "native"]
         assert ir.ops.fused_add_rms_norm.get_priority() == ["native"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("method", ["eagle", "eagle3", "dflash", "mtp"])
+def test_verify_vocab_size_raises_for_eagle_mismatch(method):
+    """eagle and eagle3 must enforce vocab-size parity like draft_model does."""
+    spec_cfg = SpeculativeConfig.__new__(SpeculativeConfig)
+    spec_cfg.method = method
+
+    target_mock = Mock()
+    target_mock.get_vocab_size.return_value = 128000
+
+    draft_mock = Mock()
+    draft_mock.get_vocab_size.return_value = 99999
+    draft_mock.hf_config = Mock(spec=[])  # no auto-attrs → draft_vocab_size absent
+
+    spec_cfg.target_model_config = target_mock
+    spec_cfg.draft_model_config = draft_mock
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="same vocabulary size"):
+        spec_cfg.verify_equal_vocab_size_if_draft_model()
+
+
+def test_verify_vocab_size_allows_eagle3_pruned_vocab():
+    """eagle3 with draft_vocab_size on hf_config signals intentional pruning."""
+    spec_cfg = SpeculativeConfig.__new__(SpeculativeConfig)
+    spec_cfg.method = "eagle3"
+
+    target_mock = Mock()
+    target_mock.get_vocab_size.return_value = 128000
+
+    draft_mock = Mock()
+    draft_mock.get_vocab_size.return_value = 8000
+    draft_mock.hf_config = Mock(spec=["draft_vocab_size"])
+    draft_mock.hf_config.draft_vocab_size = 8000
+
+    spec_cfg.target_model_config = target_mock
+    spec_cfg.draft_model_config = draft_mock
+
+    # must not raise
+    spec_cfg.verify_equal_vocab_size_if_draft_model()

@@ -1017,13 +1017,17 @@ def _verify_args(self) -> Self:
 
     def verify_equal_vocab_size_if_draft_model(self):
         if (
-            self.method == "draft_model"
+            (self.method == "draft_model" or self.use_eagle())
             and self.target_model_config is not None
             and self.draft_model_config is not None
         ):
             target_vocab_size = self.target_model_config.get_vocab_size()
             draft_vocab_size = self.draft_model_config.get_vocab_size()
-            if target_vocab_size != draft_vocab_size:
+            if (
+                target_vocab_size != draft_vocab_size
+                and getattr(self.draft_model_config.hf_config, "draft_vocab_size", None)
+                is None
+            ):
                 raise ValueError(
                     f"Target and draft model should have the same vocabulary size. "
                     f"Target model vocab_size={target_vocab_size}. "
